statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of six paths; authenticated message submission, account creation, ad placement and payment were not covered because they require credentials or consequential actions.

page.framework: Server-rendered multi-page site with React-enhanced surfaces
page.notes: Representative coverage: homepage, category/filter landing, listing detail, login, consent and not-found recovery. Excluded authenticated messaging/bidding completion, account creation, ad placement, checkout/payment and every category because they require credentials/consequential actions or duplicate audited templates.

paths.description: Homepage and search entry point; represents global navigation, discovery feed, search controls, preferences, mobile layout, performance, privacy and no-JS behavior.
Cars category landing and filter form; represents category/index pages and faceted product discovery.
Representative listing detail; covers product metadata, seller context, responsive media and contact/bid actions.
Authentication entry; represents account access and input assistance. Credential submission was intentionally not attempted.
Privacy-preferences route; represents consent and user control.
Deliberately invalid route; represents HTTP/navigation recovery and useful error state.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a white/light interface; the probe reports colorScheme "light" while (prefers-color-scheme: dark) matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Loading skeleton motion continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the probe found 40 running Skeleton-shineLines animations, each 1500 ms, and found no reduced-motion CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential shimmer/transition animation inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no authored view-transition usage, while the audited homepage, category and detail surfaces make abrupt document/state changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive View Transitions for listing/category navigation and major same-document state changes, retaining a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior relies on viewport rules rather than container-aware components.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules; DOM CSS excerpts show repeated @media(min-width:768px) rules across reusable listing/detail components.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards, carousels and filter groups containment and adapt them with container queries.

findings.summary: Cold mobile performance misses the good LCP and responsiveness bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 15.3 s, FCP 3.8 s, TBT 500 ms and performance 0.47. A separate trace measured LCP 2.93 s, showing substantial run variability but not invalidating the slow cold-load result.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce blocking script work and validate mobile field/lab LCP and INP after each change.

findings.summary: JavaScript creates avoidable main-thread work on cold load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 3.1 s main-thread work, 1.8 s JavaScript execution and 500 ms TBT; the trace still recorded a >50 ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the largest tasks, split work, schedule non-critical tasks later and avoid loading ad/analytics code before it is needed.

findings.summary: The critical path is delayed by render-blocking resources and a deep script dependency chain.
findings.evidence: The HAR summary identifies four VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheets and several parser-inserted scripts; Lighthouse estimates 1,480 ms render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical styles, defer non-critical CSS/scripts, and set explicit priority for the actual LCP resource.

findings.summary: The page ships a large amount of unused and legacy JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 801 KiB unused JavaScript plus 39 KiB legacy JavaScript; HAR records 28 scripts transferring 1.97 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by user intent and remove duplicate/legacy/unused bundles, especially analytics and advertising code from initial load.

findings.summary: Some important controls lack accessible names or have mismatched names.
findings.evidence: axe reports a critical unnamed profile/hamburger button. Lighthouse also fails button-name, aria-dialog-name and label-content-name-mismatch.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native semantics and stable visible/accessible names for every icon button and dialog; ensure aria-label matches visible control text.

findings.summary: The homepage heading and landmark structure is incomplete.
findings.evidence: axe reports no main landmark, content outside landmarks and a skipped heading level; recon also found an empty h1. Focus itself remained visibly outlined.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in main, provide a meaningful h1, and keep heading levels sequential.

findings.summary: At least one dialog-like surface is not exposed as a well-named semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails aria-dialog-name; the home recon found no native dialog or popover primitives despite dialog-like consent/overlay code.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog/popover with a programmatic name and declarative dismiss behavior for modal and transient surfaces.

findings.summary: Images are not explicitly sized in markup.
findings.evidence: The image audit found all 45 img elements without width/height attributes; Lighthouse also fails unsized-images, although observed CLS in this capture was 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or a stable aspect-ratio for every image so space is reserved before loading.

findings.summary: The page blocks back/forward cache and lacks source maps for large first-party scripts.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons and missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove avoidable no-store responses/state changes from the navigation path and publish production source maps securely for debugging.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are weaker than expected.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and SAMEORIGIN are present, but CSP is missing. Cookie audit found 11 of 12 cookies without Secure, including MpSession, and widespread SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure; use Lax/Strict unless cross-site behavior is required and documented.

findings.summary: The initial page has a very large tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 12 third-party origins and PubMatic, DoubleClick and Google ad trackers. HAR attributes 74/77 requests and 2.49 MB/2.53 MB to origins classified as third party.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential advertising/analytics behind consent and user intent, reduce vendors, batch measurement, and enforce a third-party byte/request budget.

findings.summary: The observed sign-in flow is password-led and exposes no passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login screenshot offers Google or email/password; the runtime probe found no navigator.credentials integration in the observed surface. No permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey/WebAuthn authentication and keep password fallback; request any permissions only after a user action.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS and X-Frame-Options, but no CSP, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; long-lived SameSite=None analytics cookies are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP/frame-ancestors, a strict Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; tighten cross-site cookie posture.

findings.summary: Listing images are not delivered responsively.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 43 of 45 images without srcset and all 45 without explicit dimensions; one logo was over 2x displayed width.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide responsive srcset/sizes, stable dimensions and appropriately compressed variants at the rendered size.

findings.summary: Large advertising and analytics bundles load before user intent.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 1.97 MB of script, including ~296 KB PubMatic, multiple 140–202 KB tag-manager bundles and ~201 KB ad code on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-essential advertising/analytics, consolidate measurement tags and stop background work when hidden.

findings.summary: Third-party resources dominate the page budget.
findings.evidence: Third-party-classified origins account for 2.49 MB of 2.53 MB transferred and 74 of 77 requests; Lighthouse total payload is 3,084 KiB in its run.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce per-vendor and total third-party budgets, with delayed loading and removal when value does not justify cost.

findings.summary: High-value marketplace actions are not exposed as structured agent capabilities.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no WebMCP/modelContext surface; agents must infer search, filter and listing-contact behavior from the visual DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose narrowly scoped, user-confirmed WebMCP tools for search/filtering and safe listing actions, with human review for consequential steps.
